## INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED INFECTION

[Approach to intravascular catheter-associated infection and antimicrobial](appro-intravas-cath-assoc-infect) lock therapy When catheter-related bacteremia is suspected, draw blood cultures from both the catheter and a peripheral vein. If patient is seriously ill (hypotension, hypoperfusion, signs and symptoms of organ failure) remove catheter and culture tip. In patients who are moderately ill (e.g. hypotension, organ failure), remove catheter and culture tip if patient has a prosthetic valve, pacemaker or vascular graft. Start empirical antibiotics while awaiting culture results.
Narrow therapeutic spectrum based on sensitivities of cultured pathogens.

Therapy:
**Empirical therapy**
Vancomycin Pharmacy to dose

**Empirical therapy for immunosuppressed patients**
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h ($$) R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV
q12h ($) [R]

For patients with penicillin allergy:
Vancomycin pharmacy to dose <AND> Gentamicin Pharmacy to dose
